title: PasswordResetForm
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column with a when over the steps, MonarchTextField with KeyboardType.Email, MonarchPasswordInput with the New purpose, MonarchPasswordStrengthMeter, MonarchButton and MonarchInlineNotice; an Android App Link (an intent filter with android:autoVerify) returns the link to the app
summary: A recipe, not a component: request a reset link by email, then, when the emailed link opens the app, choose a new password with a live strength meter.
whenToUse: For a 'Forgot password' flow in an app that signs people in with its own email and password.
whenNotToUse: When people sign in with Rook ID (MonarchSignInWithRookButton), Google or passkeys, the provider owns password reset; link to it instead. For changing a password while signed in, ask for the current password with MonarchPasswordInput instead of a link.
api: MonarchTextField(value = email, onValueChange = …, label = "Email", errorText = emailError, keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = KeyboardType.Email))
MonarchPasswordInput(value = password, onValueChange = …, label = "New password", purpose = MonarchPasswordInputPurpose.New)
MonarchButton(text = "Send reset link", onClick = …, modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Primary, loading = working)
<intent-filter android:autoVerify="true"> with ACTION_VIEW, BROWSABLE and the https host and path of the link; read intent.data in the activity

options.name: step
options.description: The app's state: request, sent, reset or done. Start on reset when the activity was opened by the reset link.

options.name: resetToken
options.description: The token from the App Link, read from intent.data in onCreate and onNewIntent. Sent with the new password.

options.name: working
options.description: Passed to the primary button's loading while the request or the save runs.

options.name: formError
options.description: A failed request or save, or an expired link, shown in a danger MonarchInlineNotice above the step.

states.name: request
states.description: The email field and Send reset link. An invalid address shows its error on the field.

states.name: sent
states.description: Check your email, naming the address, with a way back to use a different email.

states.name: reset
states.description: Opened by the emailed link: the new password with the strength meter and the confirmation. Change password stays disabled until every rule is met and the two match.

states.name: done
states.description: Password changed, with Back to sign in.

states.name: working
states.description: The primary button shows its progress indicator and reads "Loading" while the request or the save runs.

states.name: failed
states.description: A failed request or save, or an expired link, goes in a danger MonarchInlineNotice above the step.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component in the theme: titles in the title style, MonarchTextField and MonarchPasswordInput with their own borders and errors, the strength meter's segments, and full-width primary buttons. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web's PasswordResetForm is one component with a step prop and messages; on Android it is a recipe, as on iOS, because the steps, the network calls and the link handling belong to the app. The link returns through an Android App Link: an intent filter with android:autoVerify="true" for the https host and path, verified by a Digital Asset Links file on the site; the activity reads the token from intent.data in onCreate and onNewIntent. The web gets it from the page URL and iOS from a Universal Link. The web's resend cooldown on the sent step is not part of the recipe; MonarchEmailVerificationBanner keeps its cooldown internal today. The web moves focus to each step's heading; on Android each title has the heading semantics so TalkBack's heading navigation finds it. MonarchPasswordInput with the New purpose lets autofill services offer and save a strong password.
accessibility: Each step's title has the heading semantics.
The email and password fields are MonarchTextField and MonarchPasswordInput, so labels, errors and error semantics come from those components.
The password inputs use the New purpose, so autofill services can offer a strong password and save it.
The strength meter reads each rule as met or not met, not by color alone.
Buttons are MonarchButtons with 48dp touch targets and a Loading state while working.
edgeCases: Say that a link was sent whether or not an account exists, so the form does not reveal which addresses have accounts.
The reset step needs the token from the link; keep it in the app and send it with the new password.
A link opened after it expired should show the error on the reset step and offer to request a new one.
The link can arrive while the app is running: handle it in onNewIntent as well as onCreate.
